text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- The government is looking at measures to increase the involvement of private companies in export activities, particularly in rice, to reduce the trade deficit.
-- Vietnam has strongly condemned an explosion on Saturday in Cambodia's Sihanoukville which damaged a memorial monument for Vietnamese volunteer soldiers.
-- Laotian President Nouhak Phoumsavan will attend the Francophone summit in Hanoi in November.
-- Ho Chi Minh City authorities uncovered some 15,000 violations of cultural regulations between between February 1996 and May this year.
-- The government focused on ways to promote the production of goods for export during a cabinet meeting last week.
-- State-owned PetroVietnam exploited 3.9 million tonnes of crude oil between January and May this year.
-- The Canadian government has provided Vietnam with an aid programme worth $63,500 for social development projects.
-- Communist Party Secretary General Do Muoi attended a ceremony marking Children's Day on Sunday and called upon young people to be grateful to Uncle Ho, war martyrs and preceding generations.
-- The Customs Office has issued guidelines for implementation of the amended Foreign Investment Law.
